name: ROOT
Description: Starting the interview

name: ANXIETYROOT
Description: Opening of the interview. First ask what brought the patient in and ice-break briefly (one warm, short acknowledgement; do not keep expressing gratitude). Then screen: Have you been feeling anxious, worried, nervous, tense or afraid lately, or had episodes of panic? MET if the patient reports any anxiety, worry, nervousness, fear, panic or tension that bothers them, whatever its focus or duration. NOT MET only if the patient denies anxiety altogether, describes a normal mood, or says goodbye.

name: SUB
Description: Decide whether the patient's anxiety is primarily the direct physiological effect of a substance (alcohol, cannabis, stimulants, opioids, sedatives, hallucinogens, inhalants, nicotine or caffeine, including intoxication, hangover or withdrawal) or of a medication (e.g., corticosteroids, beta-blockers, hormonal agents, anticonvulsants, interferon, isotretinoin, benzodiazepine withdrawal). ASK: current and recent alcohol or drug use, how much and how often; any prescription medication started, stopped or changed around the time the mood changed; whether the mood is clearly worse during or after use (hangover, come-down, withdrawal). MET if the patient reports regular or heavy substance use or a medication change AND the mood disturbance is clearly tied to it: it began with the use, or it is markedly worse during intoxication, hangover or withdrawal. A patient who started drinking to cope and now finds the mood worse the day after drinking still counts as MET; do not reject it because the low mood came first. NOT MET if the patient denies relevant use, reports only occasional social drinking with no effect on mood, or describes a mood that is unchanged by use. Do not infer use the patient has not reported. If the only candidate is a medication prescribed for a medical condition that can itself cause this mood change (e.g., thyroid medication for thyroid disease), do NOT decide it here: NOT MET, and let the medical-condition node assess it.

name: SUB_DIST
Description: Determine if the patient's anxiety mood is associated with disturbance in attention and awareness is characterized by a fluctuating course. The criteria is met when there is evidence of changes in the patient's level of attention or alertness that vary over time.

name: SIDELIRIUM
Description: Substance Intoxication Delirium; Substance withdrawal delirium; Medication-Induced Delirium

name: SUB_DIST_SEV
Description: Evaluate if the anxiety mood reported by the patient is the primary focus of the clinical picture and is of sufficient severity to require clinical attention. This means the symptoms should be significant enough to cause notable distress or impairment, making them a central concern in the patient's overall condition.

name: SIANX
Description: Substance/Medication-Induced Anxiety Disorder

name: SI
Description: Substance Intoxication; Substance Withdrawal; Other Adverse Effect of Medication

name: MED
Description: Decide whether the patient's anxiety is primarily the direct physiological effect of a general medical condition (e.g., thyroid or other endocrine disorders, stroke, Parkinson's disease, multiple sclerosis, traumatic brain injury, epilepsy, heart failure, chronic pain, autoimmune disease, HIV or other infection, anemia, cancer, vitamin B12 or D deficiency, kidney or liver disease, sleep apnea). ASK: any diagnosed medical condition or recent illness; any abnormal test results; whether the mood change started with or tracks the medical problem. MET only if the patient reports such a condition AND the mood disturbance is plausibly its direct physiological consequence (onset or worsening tied to the illness). NOT MET if the patient denies any relevant medical condition, reports a normal recent check-up, or has a condition unrelated in timing to the mood change. A patient who denies medical problems is NOT MET; never infer a medical cause the patient has not reported. If the patient has a diagnosed condition known to cause this kind of mood change (e.g., hyperthyroidism for elevated mood, hypothyroidism for depression) and the mood change began or worsened after the illness started, that is MET; do not demand that a doctor explicitly linked the two.

name: MED_DIST
Description: Decide whether the patient's anxiety comes with a DISTURBANCE OF ATTENTION AND AWARENESS that fluctuates over hours or days (delirium): confusion, trouble focusing or following the conversation, disorientation, drowsiness alternating with agitation. ASK: whether the patient has had episodes of confusion or not knowing where they were, or periods when their alertness changed markedly within the day. MET only if the patient reports such fluctuating confusion or altered awareness. NOT MET if the patient is alert and oriented and describes anxiety without confusion, however severe the anxiety is; severity is assessed at the next node. A clear episode of confusion or disorientation during the course of the medical illness (e.g., while hospitalized when the condition was severe) counts as MET even if the patient is clear-headed today.

name: MEDDELIRIUM
Description: Delirium Due to Another Medical Condition

name: MED_DIST_SEV
Description: Assess whether the patient shows evidence of decline in one or more cognitive domains, including complex attention, executive function, learning and memory, language, perceptual-motor abilities, or social cognition. This decline should be noticeable and impact the patient's ability to function in these specific areas.

name: MNEUD
Description: Major or Mild Neurocognitive disorder due to another medical condition, with behavioral disturbance

name: MEDANX
Description: Anxiety Disorder Due to Another Medical Condition

name: FEAR
Description: Decide whether the patient's problem is limited to ISOLATED PANIC ATTACKS: one or a few discrete episodes of abrupt intense fear or discomfort that peak within minutes (pounding heart, sweating, shaking, shortness of breath, chest pain, dizziness, fear of dying or losing control), WITHOUT the attacks being recurrent and unexpected, and WITHOUT ongoing worry between attacks or other persistent anxiety. ASK: whether such sudden surges have occurred; how many; whether they come out of the blue or only in a specific situation; whether the patient worries or is anxious between attacks. MET if the patient has had one such attack, or a few attacks after unusual one-off circumstances (an exam, a bad night, an argument), and does NOT describe a recurring pattern of attacks out of the blue. A single attack is enough; background stress or feeling overwhelmed does not count against it. Attacks that reliably occur in ONE SPECIFIC FEARED SITUATION OR OBJECT the patient avoids (flying, heights, enclosed spaces, animals, injections, crowds, speaking in public) are the expression of that fear, not isolated attacks: NOT MET, so the fear is assessed at the later nodes. NOT MET if the attacks are recurrent and unexpected (panic disorder is assessed at the next node), if the patient's main problem is persistent worry, situational fear or other anxiety rather than isolated attacks, or if the patient has never had a sudden surge. Choose NOT MET when the patient describes repeated attacks without a trigger, or attacks bound to one feared situation.

name: PANICATTACK
Description: Panic Attack

name: PANICSEV
Description: Decide whether the patient has PANIC DISORDER: recurrent (more than one) UNEXPECTED panic attacks, i.e. abrupt surges of intense fear or discomfort peaking within minutes that come out of the blue. Persistent worry about further attacks or avoidance because of them supports the decision but is not required. ASK: how many attacks; whether they occur without an obvious trigger. MET if the patient reports more than one attack that came without a clear trigger. NOT MET if attacks are only triggered by a specific situation, if there has been only one attack, or if the patient has no panic attacks.

name: PANICDISORDER
Description: Panic Disorder

name: PLACE
Description: Decide whether the patient has AGORAPHOBIC fear: marked fear or avoidance of situations such as public transport, open spaces, enclosed places, crowds or queues, or being outside the home alone, because escape might be difficult or help unavailable if panic-like or embarrassing symptoms occurred. ASK: which situations are feared; why; whether they are avoided or endured with distress. MET only if the fear is specifically about these situations for these reasons and is the patient's main anxiety. NOT MET if the patient's anxiety is general worry, fear of social judgement, fear of a specific object, or if the situations are not avoided and the fear is not about escape or help being unavailable. Feeling tense in a cafe or meeting while worrying about the conversation is NOT agoraphobia.

name: AGORAPHOBIA
Description: Agoraphobia

name: SPERATION
Description: Decide whether the patient's anxiety is SEPARATION anxiety: excessive fear about being apart from or losing major attachment figures (harm befalling them, being separated), with reluctance to be away from them. ASK: what specifically the patient fears when apart from close people. MET only if the fear is specifically about separation from or harm to attachment figures and is the patient's primary anxiety. NOT MET if the patient's worries are general or focused elsewhere. Merely feeling calmer around trusted people or in familiar places is NOT separation anxiety.

name: SEPANX
Description: Separation Anxiety Disorder

name: SOCIAL
Description: Decide whether the patient has SOCIAL ANXIETY: marked fear of social situations in which they may be scrutinized (meeting people, conversations, being observed eating, speaking or performing), with fear of acting in a way that will be negatively judged, humiliated or rejected; the situations almost always provoke fear and are avoided or endured with intense distress. ASK: which situations; whether the fear is specifically about being judged; whether they are avoided. MET only if fear of negative evaluation in social situations is the patient's primary and consistent anxiety. NOT MET if social concern is one of many worries (work, health, money, the future, things going wrong), if the patient describes perfectionism or overthinking outcomes rather than fear of scrutiny, or if the patient still engages in social situations without avoidance. When social worry coexists with broad worry about many areas of life, choose NOT MET; generalized anxiety is assessed at a later node. Also NOT MET if the fear of being looked at is specifically about a perceived flaw in the patient's appearance (nose, skin, body shape); that concern is assessed at a later node.

name: SOCIALANX
Description: Social Anxiety Disorder

name: FEAROBJ
Description: Decide whether the patient has a SPECIFIC PHOBIA: marked fear of a particular object or situation (e.g., spiders, heights, flying, injections, blood, enclosed spaces) that is out of proportion, almost always triggered by it, and avoided. ASK: whether there is one specific thing that triggers the fear; whether it is avoided; and where the fear came from. MET if the fear is tied to a specific object or situation (flying, heights, enclosed spaces, animals, injections) and is the patient's most distinct and intense fear, even if they also report general background stress; it does not have to be their only complaint. It must not be explained by the exclusions below. NOT MET if there is no specific trigger or the anxiety is general. Also NOT MET, because they are assessed at later nodes, if the feared situation is a reminder of a traumatic event (e.g., fear of driving after an accident, with flashbacks or nightmares), if the distress is about discarding or sorting possessions, if it is about a perceived flaw in appearance, or if it is about having an illness. A fear tied to a recent life event or stressor (e.g., dread about visiting a parent who moved into a nursing home) is NOT a specific phobia either; that is assessed at a later node.

name: SPEPHOBIA
Description: Specific Phobia

name: HEALTH
Description: Decide whether the patient's anxiety is primarily about HEALTH: preoccupation with having or acquiring a serious illness. ASK: whether the main worry is about illness or bodily symptoms; whether reassurance helps. MET only if health or illness is the primary focus of the anxiety. NOT MET if health is one of several worries or is not a focus at all.

name: SOMATIC
Description: Decide whether the patient has SUBSTANTIAL PHYSICAL SYMPTOMS that are themselves present and distressing (persistent or recurring pain, stomach trouble, fatigue, dizziness, weakness) and that take up time and energy, as opposed to a fear of having a serious illness with few or only trivial bodily symptoms. ASK: what physical symptoms they actually have, how often and how strongly they occur, and whether the symptoms themselves get in the way of their day. MET if the patient describes real, recurring physical symptoms that disrupt their day or cause them real discomfort, EVEN IF they also worry a great deal about what the symptoms mean; worry about the symptoms does not count against this node. NOT MET only if bodily symptoms are absent, trivial or fleeting (a twinge, a flutter, a minor headache) and the complaint is almost entirely the fear of having a disease, checking the body, searching symptoms or seeking reassurance: that pattern is illness anxiety and is handled by the next node.

name: SOMATICD
Description: Somatic Symptom Disorder

name: SEV_PHYS
Description: Determine if the patient's belief about having a serious physical illness reaches a delusional intensity. The criteria is met when the conviction is strongly held despite clear evidence to the contrary.

name: PSYCHD
Description: Psychotic Disorder

name: ILLANX
Description: Illness Anxiety Disorder

name: DISCARD
Description: Check if the patient feels anxious about getting rid of personal items, leading to a buildup of possessions that clutter their living spaces. The criteria is met when this anxiety makes it hard to let go of items, causing clutter that affects daily living.

name: HOARDINGD
Description: Hoarding Disorder

name: APPEARANCE
Description: Check if the patient feels anxious or worried about a perceived flaw in their appearance that is not noticeable to others. The criteria is met when the concern about this imagined defect causes significant distress.

name: BODYDD
Description: Body Dysmorphic Disorder

name: REC
Description: Decide whether the patient's anxiety consists of PERSISTENT WORRY or REPETITIVE THOUGHTS. ASK: what the patient worries about; whether worry is present most days; whether it is hard to control; whether it comes with restlessness, fatigue, poor concentration, irritability, muscle tension or sleep problems. MET if the patient reports persistent, hard-to-control worry about several areas of life, or repetitive intrusive thoughts, present more days than not and distressing. NOT MET if anxiety is limited to discrete attacks or to a specific situation already excluded, or the patient denies ongoing worry. NOT MET, because it is assessed at a later node, if the repetitive thoughts are memories, flashbacks or nightmares of a traumatic event such as an accident or assault.

name: INTRUSIVE
Description: Decide whether the thoughts are OBSESSIONS: recurrent intrusive, unwanted thoughts, urges or images that feel senseless or against the patient's own values, which the patient tries to suppress or neutralize, often with compulsions (checking, washing, counting, repeating). ASK: whether the thoughts feel unwanted and senseless rather than realistic concerns; whether there are rituals. MET only if the patient reports such ego-dystonic intrusions or compulsions. NOT MET if the worry is about realistic everyday concerns (work, family, health, finances, the future) even when excessive and hard to control; that pattern is generalized anxiety.

name: OBSESSIVE
Description: Obsessive-complusive Disorder

name: GENERALIZEDANX
Description: Generalized Anxiety Disorder

name: TRAUMA
Description: Check if the patient experiences anxiety related to exposure to a severe traumatic event, accompanied by intrusive symptoms (such as flashbacks or nightmares), avoidance of reminders of the trauma, negative changes in thoughts and mood, and increased arousal or reactivity. The criteria is met when these symptoms are present and cause significant distress.

name: TRAUMA_DUR
Description: Criteria met if the patient's stress disorder symptoms last more than a month, the duration should be explicitly asked

name: PTSD
Description: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder

name: ASD
Description: Acute Stress Disorder

name: MANIC
Description: Check if the patient experiences anxiety that is associated with a manic episode, a hypomanic episode, or a major depressive episode. The criteria is met when the anxiety occurs alongside one of these mood episodes and causes significant distress.

name: MDDANX
Description: Major Depressive Episode with Anxious feawtures in major depressive, bipolar I, or BipolarII disorder

name: OTH
Description: Decide whether the anxiety is an OVER-REACTION TO EVERYDAY DEMANDS without a single identifiable life event: the patient is overwhelmed by small routine stressors (an email from the boss, errands, deadlines), reacts out of proportion and avoids them, but cannot point to one specific recent change in their life that started it. ASK: whether there was one particular event or change that set the anxiety off, or whether it is the pile of everyday demands. MET if it is the everyday pile with no single event. NOT MET if the anxiety began after one identifiable life event (a move, a loss, a relative's illness, a breakup, a job change), which is assessed at the next node, or if the anxiety is mild and proportionate.

name: PSYCHSTRESSOR
Description: Check if the patient's symptoms occur in response to a psychosocial stressor. The criteria is met when the anxiety or distress is directly linked to a specific life event or stressor.

name: NORMALANX
Description: Decide whether the anxiety is an ADJUSTMENT REACTION: it began within about 3 months of one identifiable life event or change (a parent moving into care, a move, a loss, a breakup) and is out of proportion to it or interferes with functioning. ASK: what happened around the time the anxiety started; how much it dominates the patient's thoughts. MET if there is such an event and the reaction is out of proportion or impairing. NOT MET if no identifiable event can be named, or the reaction is proportionate and short-lived.

name: ADJD
Description: Adjustment Disorder With Anxiety

name: OTHANX
Description: Other specified anxiety disorder; Unspecified anxiety disorder

name: NORMAL
Description: No Anxiety Mood
